To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IRS-2 is upregulated in the regenerating pancreas of 60%-pancreatectomy rat model and that IRS-2 and phospho-Akt expression are associated with the proliferation of the common duct epithelia and differentiation into insulin-producing beta cell, respectively.
IRS-2 is involved in the early stages of pancreatic regeneration and that Akt plays a role in the later stages.

IRS-2 expression is upregulated in regenerating common duct epithelum of the rat pancreas after partial pancreatectomies and that this upregulation is associated with activation of Akt, a protein kinase involved in cell growth and survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of pancreatic beta cell regeneration.
the role of IRS-2 and its associated signaling pathways in the process of regeneration of the pancreas.
the role of IRS-2 in pancreatic regeneration and adaptation to beta cell mass loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin and IGF-I play a major role in the regulation of beta-cell mass, and that the insulin receptor and IRS-2 may be the key mediators of this process.
IRS2 plays an important and significant role in the process of pancreatic regeneration.
insulin signaling through the insulin receptor substrate 2 and protein kinase B (Akt) is involved in the regeneration process of the pancreas following partial pancreatecctomy in rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IRS-2 is a major player in the process of pancreatic regeneration and growth.
IRS-2 is a major regulator of beta cell mass and function.
the IRS-2 and phospho-Akt proteins have important roles in the regulation of early pancreatic regeneration and growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IRS-2 is an essential component of the early compensatory mechanisms that occur in response to partial pancreatectomies.
insulin and its receptor and signaling proteins are not just for the beta cells but also for the duct cells and that the ducts play an important role in regeneration.

IRS-2 and phospho-Akt are expressed in the common duct evagination of the rat pancreas following partial pancreatec-tomy, suggesting that they may play an important role in the early events of pancreatic regeneration and growth.
